laus.filter: dimensions.survey == LAUS and subject geo:US:county:* and period_type == month

qcew.filter: dimensions.survey == QCEW and dimensions.agglvl_code == 70 (county, total covered, all ownerships) and period_type == annual_average

controls.definition: same-state counties never treated or first treated after max(t, g-1); never the cohort itself

estimator.estimand: ATT: equal-weight mean over event times 0..5 of treated-count-weighted ATT(g, g+e)

inference.bootstrap_weights: rademacher multiplier on state influence functions

primary.label: log QCEW annual-average covered employment (county, total covered, all ownerships)

secondary.label: log CBP establishments (2019-2023 only; exploratory, underpowered)
secondary.source: census_business CBP county establishment_count, all industries

outcomes.transform: natural log of positive values; suppressed or missing values dropped

placebo_date.definition: treated counties keep only years before g; placebo cohort g-3; placebo effect averaged over placebo event times 0..2

placebo_unit.definition: real treated counties removed; never-treated counties get cohorts drawn from their state's real cohorts at the state's real treated share

design.question: When a US county enters its first physical-hazard FEMA major disaster (DR) after at least five disaster-free years, how do its covered employment and establishment counts change over the following five years, relative to same-state counties not yet hit?

treatment.absorbing: later declarations in a treated county are part of its post-period treatment path
treatment.baseline_quiet_period: counties with any qualifying DR incident beginning 1990-1994 are excluded from the study
treatment.excluded_incident_types: Biological (COVID-19 declared every county in 2020), Drought (slow onset, no shock date), Terrorist, Chemical, Toxic Substances, Human Cause, Fishing Losses, Other
treatment.later_cohorts: counties first treated 2020-2024 are not-yet-treated controls until treated
treatment.timing: cohort g = calendar year of incident_begin_date of the county's first qualifying DR with incident_begin_date in 1995-2024; the declaration date is not used because the physical shock precedes it

units.definition: US counties and county equivalents in the 50 states and DC (state FIPS <= 56), identified by 5-digit FIPS as published by QCEW
units.notes: County definitional changes are not bridged; a county contributes to a group-time cell only when it has the outcome at both t and the base period
units.strata: state (2-digit FIPS): every comparison is within state

overall.definition: equal-weight mean of ATT(e) over the post event times listed

outcome.label: log QCEW annual-average covered employment (county, total covered, all ownerships)

overall.definition: equal-weight mean of ATT(e) over the post event times listed
equal-weight mean of ATT(e) over the post event times listed
equal-weight mean of stacked ATT(e) over post event times

twfe_static.warning: biased under staggered adoption with heterogeneous or dynamic effects; comparison only

assumptions: Parallel trends: absent treatment, the average outcome of treated units would have moved like that of the comparison units (not-yet-treated or never-treated, within stratum when stratified) from the base period on.
No anticipation beyond the registered anticipation window: outcomes before g - anticipation do not respond.
Absorbing treatment: the first qualifying event defines the cohort; later events are part of the post-period treatment path, so estimates are effects of entering treatment, not of one isolated event.
SUTVA / no interference: a unit's outcome does not depend on other units' treatment (spillovers to comparison units bias the estimate toward zero or away from it).
Treatment timing is recorded correctly by the source date the registration names.

Within a state, the timing of a county's first qualifying disaster after a quiet period is as good as random with respect to its employment trend (weather and geology, not local economic conditions, determine which quiet county is hit first).
Declaration itself is part of the treatment: the estimand is the combined effect of the physical disaster and the federal assistance a DR declaration unlocks; the two are not separated.
Spillovers to same-state comparison counties (displaced workers, reconstruction demand) are small relative to the direct effect.
Selection into the sample (no qualifying DR in 1990-1994) does not interact with treatment effects in a way that changes their sign.
identification.estimand: ATT: equal-weight mean over event times 0..5 of treated-count-weighted ATT(g, g+e)
identification.label: did_failed_diagnostics
identification.meaning: A difference-in-differences estimate whose pre-registered diagnostics failed. It is reported for transparency and must not be read as an intervention response.

results.verdict: No causal claim. Pre-registered diagnostics failed (no_pre_trends, placebo_date_null), so the parallel-trends design is not credible here. The estimate for log QCEW annual-average covered employment (county, total covered, all ownerships), +0.0092 log points (95% CI -0.0090 to +0.0275), is reported only for transparency.
